What the records reach, and where they come from
How much of the manuscript tradition the open catalogues hold, and the sources behind every record on this page.
HOW FAR THE OPEN DATA REACHES

The open data holds about 31% of the Greek New Testament manuscripts in the official register, but nearly all of the oldest: 95% of the papyri and 90% of the majuscules. Most of what is missing is mediaeval. Another catalogue we consulted does not allow its records to be republished, so nothing from it is shown.

Only 75 of the 1,571 Greek Old Testament records carry a date; most are a catalogue number alone. The 954 scroll records give where each was found but no present holder; 439 of them carry a date, most of them the period of their script.
